chunks: And in the narration of ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said:
"The one performing iʿtikāf in Makkah may perform salat (prayer) in whichever of its houses he wishes; it is the same for him whether he performs salat (prayer) in the mosque or in its houses."

key_terms.بُيُوتِهَا: its houses, meaning the houses of Makkah
key_terms.بِمَكَّةَ: in Makkah, the sacred city in which this ruling applies
key_terms.سَوَاءٌ عَلَيْهِ: it is the same for him, indicating no legal distinction in this matter
key_terms.ٱلْمَسْجِدِ: the mosque, contrasted here with the houses of Makkah
key_terms.ٱلْمُعْتَكِفُ: the person observing iʿtikāf, a spiritual retreat

ai.seo_question: Can a person in iʿtikāf in Makkah pray outside the mosque in its houses?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning iʿtikāf in Makkah. It states that for the muʿtakif, performing salat (prayer) in the houses of Makkah carries the same ruling as performing it in the mosque.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2092 - In a narration from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah (as), it is reported:
"The one performing i'tikaf in Mecca may pray in any of its houses; it is the same whether they pray in the mosque or in its houses."
